messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH p95/p99 latency SLO burn — eu-west-1 inference cluster. rule: \"p95 > 350ms for 5m\". Pager: oncall@redwood.com :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-202379 opened and routed to schedule 'eng-oncall'. Paging: maria, then ben if no ack in 2m.

maria (oncall): acked. I'm looking. first check: dashboards show p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s, error rates low.

sahil (sre): noted. Any recent deploys? logs show a routing spike at 12:03 UTC, lots of reroutes between model-v1 and model-v1-quant.

maria (oncall): yes there was an autoscale config tweak for routing weights earlier today. I'm pulling routing history.

ben (infra): on my way, can we repro with a small load test? also checking sidecar queue backpressure stats.

maria (oncall): stacktrace/nodes: most tail latency coming from hotpath inference pods in eu-west-1a. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 45% around spike.

sahil (sre): low KV hit explains token compute increase. Could be cache eviction due to sudden prefix pattern shift. Any traffic spikes?

maria (oncall): traffic stable, but routing jitter sent 30% more requests to v1 (bigger model) vs v1-quant. weight controller logs: race on rollout causing oscillation.

ben (infra): if controller is oscillating, it will thrash warm caches. I'm temporarily pinning traffic to v1-quant to reduce per-token latency. Doing now: `kubectl patch configmap routing -p '{\"spec\":{\"pin\":\"v1-quant\"}}'`

maria (oncall): saw the patch. routing stabilized. p95 dropping to 320ms after 40s. still higher than target.

sahil (sre): let's also lift per-node concurrency to relieve queueing while cache warms. bumping sidecar max-conns from 40 -> 60 for eu-west pods.

ben (infra): applied. watch logs: sidecar queue length dropping, per-pod cpu up but within headroom. p99 moved to 780ms -> 540ms.

maria (oncall): customer impact: small increase in latency for a 10-15m window for EU customers; error rates OK. Logging an incident impact note for SOC.

sahil (sre): will follow up with autoscaler + routing controller owners. Need a postmortem on unstable rollout logic.

maria (oncall): I want to enable fallback policy to smallest compatible variant for latency-sensitive routes: `routing.policy.fallback = v1-quant-small` — proposing to enable for 10m as temporary mitigation.

ben (infra): approved. enabling fallback on production traffic routes now.

maria (oncall): fallback enabled. p95 at 280ms, p99 ~420ms. This should meet SLOs.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-202379 acknowledged by maria (oncall).

sahil (sre): I'm creating a quick alert suppression window so we don't autopage while we validate. Setting suppression for 15m.

maria (oncall): creating ticket: SRE-4567 with notes and commands used. tagging owners: @ben, @taylor (routing), @leo (model-onboarding).

ben (infra): thanks — I'll roll a small config fix to the routing controller to add hysteresis on weight changes to avoid oscillation. will stage in canary.

maria (oncall): good. will keep monitoring for 30m then handoff to next oncall. Current plan: keep fallback enabled for 10m, then remove and observe; if oscillation repeats escalate to oncall rotation lead.

sahil (sre): postmortem checklist: routing controller race, KV cache eviction thresholds, autoscaler headroom defaults, alert thresholds tuning.

maria (oncall): final check: p95 at 260ms, p99 at 390ms. marking incident as mitigated. I'll close when suppression ends and metrics stable for 15m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-202379 status changed: mitigated (ack still held).

maria (oncall): handing off at 13:12 UTC to ben for follow-up and postmortem. leaving runbook notes in SRE-4567.

ben (infra): taking handoff. will follow up with a corrective config PR and link it here. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Reminder: create postmortem within 48h and set severity label.

maria (oncall): thanks — closing operational thread once postmortem link added.
